standard_prerequisites: Impurities above a point as witnesses of impurity, and the base change of the relative assassin of a module
The reduced induced structure on the closure of a point, and its behaviour under a directed limit of the base
Quasi-compactness of the fibres of a morphism of finite type, and the criterion that a directed limit of quasi-compact spaces is nonempty exactly when some stage is
core_obligations: Unwind the notation of the statement: the points of the limit project to points of each stage and the chosen point of the total space maps to points of the base changed spaces
Use base change of the relative assassin to see that the projected point still lies in the relative assassin of the base changed module, so that only the closure condition remains to be checked

Realise the closures of the chosen points at every stage as a directed limit, take the fibre over the given point of the base, and observe that the fibre is empty because the impurity kills it, while each stage's fibre is quasi-compact because the morphisms are of finite type

Apply the nonemptiness criterion for limits of quasi-compact spaces to conclude that some stage has empty fibre, which means that the projected point is not in the image of the closure, so that the projection of the impurity at that stage is an impurity
proof_roadmap: Project the impurity to each stage and use base change of the relative assassin
Express the closures as a limit and take the fibre over the point of the base
Use quasi-compactness and the nonemptiness criterion to find a stage with empty fibre
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the descent of an impurity to a stage of a directed limit of affine schemes at source lines 318-326, label lemma-impure-limit, whose proof occupies source lines 328-360. The proof proceeds in two independent steps: it first uses base change of the relative assassin to verify that the projected point remains an associated point of the base changed module, reducing the claim to the closure condition, and then handles the closure condition by realising the closures of the chosen points over the stages as a directed limit, taking the fibre over the given point of the base, and observing that this fibre is empty at the limit but quasi-compact at each stage, so that the nonemptiness criterion for limits of quasi-compact spaces produces a stage where the fibre is already empty. The counted statement records neither the relative assassin step nor the limit criterion.
